The second author was partially suppor
arxiv-2109-06487.creator: Kam Hang Cheng, Yik Man Chiang, Avery Ching
arxiv-2109-06487.description: Abstract . We establish analogues of Liouville’s theorem in the complex function theory, with the differential operator replaced by various difference operators. This is done generally by the extraction of (formal) Taylor coefficients using a residue map which measures the obstruction having local “anti-derivative”.

arxiv-2205-13767.title: Fourfold anisotropic magnetoresistance of L1 0 FePt due to relaxation time anisotropy
arxiv-2205-13767.creator: Y. Dai, Y. W. Zhao, L. Ma, M. Tang, X. P. Qiu, Y. Liu, Z. Yuan, S. M. Zhou
arxiv-2205-13767.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Y. Dai, Y. W. Zhao, L. Ma, M. Tang, X. P. Qiu, Y. Liu, Z. Yuan, S. M. Zhou. Experimental measurements show that the angular dependence of the anisotropic magnetoresistance (AMR) in L1 0 ordered FePt epitaxial films on the current orientation and magnetization direction is a superposition of the corresponding dependences of twofold and fourfold symmetries.

arxiv-2207-06385.title: Unit Reducible Fields and Perfect Unary Forms
arxiv-2207-06385.creator: Alar Leibak, Christian Porter, Cong Ling
arxiv-2207-06385.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alar Leibak, Christian Porter, Cong Ling. In this paper, we introduce the notion of unit reducibility for number fields, that is, number fields in which all positive unary forms attain their nonzero minimum at a unit. Furthermore, we investigate the link between unit reducibility and the number of homothety classes of perfect unary forms for a given number field, and prove an open conjecture about the number of classes of perfect unary forms in real quadratic fields, stated by D.

arxiv-2210-11693.title: Amos : An Adam-style Optimizer with Adaptive Weight Decay towards Model-Oriented Scale
arxiv-2210-11693.creator: Ran Tian, Ankur P. Parikh
arxiv-2210-11693.description: Abstract We present Amos , a stochastic gradient-based optimizer designed for training deep neural networks. It can be viewed as an Adam optimizer with theoretically supported, adaptive learning-rate decay and weight decay. A key insight behind Amos is that it leverages model-specific information to determine the initial learning-rate and decaying schedules.

arxiv-2302-04350.title: ONE-PARAMETER FAMILIES OF CONFORMAL MAPPINGS OF THE HALF-PLANE ONTO POLYGONAL DOMAINS WITH SEVERAL SLITS
arxiv-2302-04350.creator: A. Posadskii, S. Nasyrov
arxiv-2302-04350.description: Abstract . Among various methods of finding accessory parameters in the Schwarz-Christoffel integrals, Kufarev’s method, based on the Loewner differential equation, plays an important role. It is used for describing one-parameter families of functions that conformally map a canonical domain onto a polygon with a slit the endpoint of which moves along a polygonal line starting from a boundary point.

arxiv-2401-05902.title: Optimized Asymmetric Feedback Detection for Rate-adaptive HARQ with Unreliable Feedback
arxiv-2401-05902.creator: Weihang Ding 1 and Mohammad Shikh-Bahaei 1
arxiv-2401-05902.description: Abstract This work considers downlink incremental redundancy Hybrid Automatic Repeat Request (IR-HARQ) over unreliable feedback channels. Since the impact of positive feedback (i.e., ACK) error is smaller than that of negative feedback (i.e., NACK) error, an asymmetric feedback detection scheme is proposed to protect NACK and further reduce the outage probability.

arxiv-2411-04700.title: Field Assessment of Force Torque Sensors for Planetary Rover Navigation
arxiv-2411-04700.creator: Levin Gerdes, Carlos Pérez del Pulgar, Raúl Castilla Arquillo, Martin Azkarate
arxiv-2411-04700.description: Abstract Proprioceptive sensors on planetary rovers serve for state estimation and for understanding terrain and locomotion performance. While inertial measurement units (IMUs) are widely used to this effect, force-torque sensors are less explored for planetary navigation despite their potential to directly measure interaction forces and provide insights into traction performance.

arxiv-2502-19541.title: Permuton limits for some permutations avoiding a single pattern
arxiv-2502-19541.creator: Kaitlyn Hohmeier and Erik Slivken
arxiv-2502-19541.description: Abstract Abstract Permutons are probability measures on the unit square with uniform marginals that provide a natural way to describe limits of permutations. We are interested in the permuton limits for permutations sampled uniformly from certain pattern-avoiding classes that are in bijection with the class of permutations avoiding an increasing pattern of fixed length.

arxiv-2504-17651.title: Practical aspects of the virtual noise convex optimum design approach for correlated responses
arxiv-2504-17651.creator: Markus Hainy
arxiv-2504-17651.description: Abstract Abstract: In this paper we present several practically-oriented extensions and considerations for the virtual noise method in optimal design under correlation. First we introduce a slightly modified virtual noise representation which further illuminates the parallels to the classical design approach for uncorrelated observations. We suggest more efficient algorithms to obtain the design measures.

arxiv-2508-14980.title: Paired-Sampling Contrastive Framework for Joint Physical-Digital Face Attack Detection
arxiv-2508-14980.creator: Andrei Balykin, Anvar Ganiev, Denis Kondranin, Kirill Polevoda, Nikolai Liudkevich, Artem Petrov
arxiv-2508-14980.description: Abstract Modern face recognition systems remain vulnerable to spoofing attempts, including both physical presentation attacks and digital forgeries. Traditionally, these two attacks vectors have been addressed by separate models or pipelines, each targeted to its specific artifacts and modalities. However, maintaining distinct detectors leads to increased system complexity, higher inference latency, and a combined attack vectors.

arxiv-2509-25840.title: A Multimode Classical Hierarchical Fokker–Planck Equations Approach to Molecular Vibrations: Simulating Two-Dimensional Spectra
arxiv-2509-25840.creator: Ryotaro Hoshino, Yoshitaka Tanimura
arxiv-2509-25840.description: Abstract The multimode Brownian model with nonlinear system-bath coupling offers a flexible framework for studying both intra- and intermolecular vibrational modes in condensed-phase molecular systems. This approach allows us to calculate linear and nonlinear spectra of molecular vibrations and to examine thermal effects—such as anharmonicity, energy relaxation, and dephasing—as reflected in the spectral peak profiles.

pmc-11453699.title: 7705 Paliperidone Induced Central Adrenal Insufficiency: A Case Report
pmc-11453699.creator: Inga Shevtsova, Steven J Gerstner
pmc-11453699.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Introduction: Atypical antipsychotics reduce ACTH and control secretion in healthy subjects. However, the clinical significance of it is still unclear with only a few case reports tying antipsychotics to clinically relevant adrenal insufficiency. Case: A 32-year-old male with schizoaffective and polysubstance abuse disorders was admitted to a hospital with a complex right hand infection complicated by MRSA bacteremia, and native mitral and tricuspid valves infective endocarditis.

pmc-11510820.title: The Influence of Conditions of Polycondensation in Acid Medium on the Structure of Oligosilsesquioxanes with a Novel Eugenol-Containing Substituent
pmc-11510820.creator: Alexander D Ageenkov, Nikolay S Bredov, Anna A Shcherbina, Ramil R Khasbiullin, Anton S Tupikov, Mikhail A Soldatov, Bogdan Marciniec
pmc-11510820.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Eugenol-containing oligoorganosilsesquioxanes were synthesized by the method of hydrolytic polycondensation in an active medium under various reaction conditions. The obtained products were characterized by 29Si NMR spectroscopy and MALDI-TOF spectrometry. It was shown that factors such as the reaction temperature, polycondensation duration, and molar ratio between the initial alkoxysilane monomer and acetic acid may affect the molecular weight characteristics and molecular structure of the formed oligomer, like the content of stressed cyclic units (T3, DTT, TDT) and unstressed silsesquioxane units TnDm.

pmc-11580681.title: How to write an effective journal peer review using a staged writing approach: a best-practice guide for early-career researchers
pmc-11580681.creator: Ella T August, Andrew F Brouwer
pmc-11580681.description: Journal peer review is a gatekeeper in the scientific process, determining which papers are published in academic journals. It also supports authors in improving their papers before they go to press. Training for early-career researchers on how to conduct a high-quality peer review is scarce, however, and there are concerns about the quality of peer review in the health sciences.

pmc-11640028.title: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Human Papillomavirus Status Prediction for Oropharyngeal Cancer: A Scoping Review
pmc-11640028.creator: Andrea Migliorelli, Marianna Manuelli, Andrea Ciorba, Francesco Stomeo, Stefano Pelucchi, Chiara Bianchini
pmc-11640028.description: Simple SummaryThis review elucidates the manner in which artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the diagnosis and staging of squamous cell carcinomas of the oropharynx (OPSCC). The review examines the potential utilization of AI in discerning the status of human papillomavirus (HPV) in OPSCCs. AI is primarily employed in the analysis of imaging data and the interpretation of histological specimens.

pmc-12534407.title: ORBITaL-Net: A labeled training library for large-scale building feature extraction
pmc-12534407.creator: Benjamin Swan, Joe Pyle, Darrell Roddy, H. Lexie Yang, Amy Rose, Melanie Laverdiere
pmc-12534407.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Over the course of several years, nearly 1.5 million building outlines have been created from approximately 128,000 training tiles covering roughly 7,000 km2 of very high-resolution multispectral overhead imagery, primarily dated between 2010 and 2020. This dataset, dubbed the Oak Ridge Building Image and TrAining Label Net (ORBITaL-Net), is designed for machine learning applications and is global in scope, with samples drawn from 72 countries across North America, South America, Africa, Europe, and Asia.

pmc-12730096.title: Effects of Bentonite, Zeolite, and Illite as Dietary Supplements for Pacific White Shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei)
pmc-12730096.creator: Soohwan Kim, Seong-Mok Jeong, Hyun Mi Jung, Sara Lee, Seunghan Lee, Hyon-Sob Han, Yun Wang
pmc-12730096.description: Simple SummaryShrimp farming is a major part of aquaculture, but maintaining shrimp health and maximizing growth are ongoing challenges. In this study, we tested three natural minerals—bentonite, zeolite, and illite—as feed additives to improve the health and growth of Pacific white shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei). These minerals are known to help with digestion and immunity in animals.

pmc-13246712.title: Why health apps fail: the role of smartphone proficiency in mHealth resistance
pmc-13246712.creator: Satoshi Inagaki, Kenji Kato, Hisafumi Yasuda
pmc-13246712.description: BackgroundMobile health apps offer significant potential for health promotion, yet initial adoption remains limited. While prior research has identified app-specific barriers, the perceived usefulness (PU) and psychological resistance toward health apps compared to everyday commercial apps, as well as the foundational role of users’ smartphone proficiency, remain understudied.

pmc-13534657.creator: Takumi Kuwata, Yuusuke Murakami, Daisuke Sato, Kazuo Fujiwara, Masamichi Ikeguchi
pmc-13534657.description: Ferritins are proteins consisting of 24 subunits that make a spherical cage structure. We prepared a series of net-charge mutants of Escherichia coli and Pseudo-nitzschia multiseries ferritins (EcFtn and PmFtn, respectively) in which glutamate (Glu) and aspartate (Asp) residues located at the outer surface of the cage were substituted with glutamine and asparagine or vice versa.
